name: cluster
description: A wrapping inline row — tag rows, button rows, meta rows. Children flow along one line and reflow onto the next when they run out of room, with no breakpoint involved; gap, alignment and justification are responsive on the canon tiers

push.description: Written on a CHILD of the cluster, never the root: that child — and everything after it — is pushed to the far end of the row (margin-inline-start: auto). The "actions on the right" idiom, and logical, so it is the far end in RTL too.

a11y.notes: Layout-only primitive; no semantic role required. Wrapping is visual only — the DOM order is the reading order at every width, so a cluster never reorders content away from the sequence a screen reader announces.

notes: Reach for cluster before any breakpoint when the requirement is "these things sit in a row and may reflow": the wrap is intrinsic, so it is correct at widths nobody tested (FAQIR-SPEC §15 doctrine 1).

cluster vs stack: a horizontal stack is a row that holds its line — use it when the items must stay together and the container guarantees the room. cluster is the row that is allowed to break, which is what a tag list, a button bar or a meta line actually wants.

cluster vs switcher: cluster reflows item by item as space runs out; switcher flips the whole row to a column at one measured threshold. Choose cluster when the items are independent, switcher when they are peers that should share a line or none at all.
